title: Spiking Discrepancy Transformer for Point Cloud Analysis
claim: A hierarchical network is built from local and global stages of specialized attention and neuron modules, each detailed in zoomed-in component views.
layout: Top full-width pipeline, bottom row of 5 zoomed component panels with legend
description: A two-tier architecture figure. The top band shows a left-to-right pipeline inside a dashed rounded box. A grey airplane point cloud enters Linear, then a Local Stage (xI) of SSU, SEDA with Spiking Linear, and Spiking MLP. A Global Stage (xI) follows with SSU, SIDA with Spiking Linear, and Spiking MLP. Spiking neurons are drawn over an airplane outline, then Spiking MLP and Linear. Dashed grey skip arrows loop under the stages. Colored vertical blocks mark modules: yellow, pink, teal, blue. The bottom row zooms into each component. It shows Spiking Linear and Spiking MLP, the Spiking Sub-sampling Unit with FPS-KNN, AP and MP branches, the SEDA diagram with Q, K and V spike grids, and the SIDA diagram with summed Q and K and V. A legend at the right explains the symbols: neuron, spiking discrepancy, matrix multiply and element-wise multiply.
caption: The overview of Spiking Discrepancy Transformer and illustration of key components.
abstract: Spiking Transformer has sparked growing interest, with the Spiking Self-Attention merging spikes with self-attention to deliver both energy efficiency and competitive performance. However, existing work primarily focuses on 2D visual tasks, and in the domain of 3D point clouds, the disorder and complexity of spatial information, along with the scale of the point clouds, present significant challenges. For point clouds, we introduce spiking discrepancy, measuring differences in spike features to highlight key information, and then construct the Spiking Discrepancy Attention Mechanism (SDAM). SDAM contains two variants: the Spiking Element Discrepancy Attention captures local geometric correlations between central points and neighboring points, while the Spiking Intensity Discrepancy Attention characterizes structural patterns of point clouds based on macroscopic spike statistics. Moreover, we propose a Spatially-Aware Spiking Neuron. Based on these, we construct a hierarchical Spiking Discrepancy Transformer. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance within the Spiking Neural Networks and exhibits impressive performance compared to Artificial Neural Networks along with a few parameters and significantly lower theoretical energy consumption.
